regime.read: Risk-on by level, defensive by composition; call is risk-on but UNCONFIRMED and event-gated. GREEN, VIX 17.5, contango. The markets that speak first show no stress (bonds, credit, copper all firm). But this is a rotation tape, not a momentum-leadership advance: S&P 500 is +0.71% in 20d (+5.51% in 63d), Technology is Weakening, and all 8 sectors graded DEPLOY/HOLD read 'Momentum Fading'. Event gate: FOMC 10-28 14:00 ET, then Core PCE, GDP and claims 10-29 08:30 ET.
regime.momentum_caveat: Hurst and trend are NOT in this packet (regime block carries vix and level only), so I cannot call TRENDING vs MEAN_REVERT and will not infer it. Proxy evidence leans mean-reverting at sector level: leaders decelerate (divergence -2.5 to -10.5 across the 8 graded sectors) while beaten-down themes bounce. Dealer gamma is negative with spot below the flip, so moves are amplified both ways: every momentum entry carries whipsaw risk until the S&P 500 ETF reclaims 774.63.

differs_on: Source of risk: bonds, credit and gold do not corroborate stress (credit above 20d avg, gold falling). I read this as event risk plus fragile internals (FOMC/PCE/GDP, negative gamma, fading leaders), not credit-led stress.
Strength of the stress call: it is met on a thin margin (gap 1.28% over its elevated line, +0.51 in 20d); one soft print flips it. I treat it as a caution flag.
Divergence: 9 warnings lit but RSI type only; I weight a single-type readout low.
Macro overlay: six sectors get TAILWIND, including Technology and Communication Services, but price says Weakening and Lagging. I discount those two until RRG confirms.
Goldilocks label: with oil +14.32% in 20d and a bid dollar I would call the scenario a transition, not disinflation-clean.
Positioning (as of 10-20, 8 days stale) predates the latest oil and bond moves; I treat crowding as dated.

what_would_change_it: Toward lighter: credit turns down while bonds keep rising (credit-confirmed stress); or the S&P 500 ETF loses the 755 put wall (1.90% below).
Toward lighter: equal-weight over cap-weight falls back through its 20d average (1.96% below), ending the broadening call.
Toward lighter: Russell 2000 loses its 2808.64 flip (0.61% below), or oil extends while the dollar keeps rising into a hot PCE.
Toward normal/aggressive: S&P 500 ETF reclaims 774.63 (gamma flips to stabilizing) and clears FOMC and PCE without a credit or dollar shock.
Toward normal/aggressive: Technology moves from WEAKENING to IMPROVING and Semiconductors / Chip Equipment leave the lagging side.
Toward normal/aggressive: oil rolls over, which would make the disinflation scenario clean rather than contested.
Hurst and trend, once served, could move the momentum caveat either way.
